text:
The issue seems to be in lines 32-33: `elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width:`.
This condition checks if adding the next word (plus a space) is *strictly less than* the width.
If the total length is exactly equal to the width, it incorrectly starts a new line (lines 34-36).
To fix this, I should change the condition to `len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width`.

I will use `edit_file` to make this change.

text:
The tests passed. I can now submit the changes.
The issue was that the `wrap` function's condition for adding a word to the current line was too strict (`< width` instead of `<= width`). This caused lines to be one character shorter than the specified width when the total length would have been exactly the width. I changed the condition to `<=` to allow lines to be exactly `width` characters long, fixing the issue.
